samples.summary: New `isEmptyStoredColor` dereferences an untrusted `StoredColor` without a type guard — a `null` color or an `{ kind: 'srgb', value: <non-string> }` persisted through the content PUT API throws a TypeError inside the paint path, crashing the renderer for every viewer of the document (stored DoS).
samples.evidence: `isEmptyStoredColor` (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:59-63) does `if (c === undefined) return false;` then `typeof c === 'string' ? ... : c.kind === 'srgb' && c.value.trim() === ''`. For `c === null` (typeof 'object', not undefined) it evaluates `c.kind` → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`. For `{ kind: 'srgb', value: 42 }` it evaluates `(42).trim()` → `TypeError: c.value.trim is not a function`. Before this delta the same input was harmless: `resolve(c === '' ? undefined : c)` passed `null` straight to the resolver, and slides' `makeColorResolver` (packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:55) returns the theme text color for `c == null`, while `resolveColor` (packages/slides/src/model/theme.ts:102) returns a non-string `value` verbatim without throwing. Attack path: an authenticated caller (workspace member or API key) PUTs a slides body to `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:ws/documents/:id/content`; `assertValidSlidesBody`/`assertValidElement` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:415-435) validate only `id`/`type`/`frame`, and `writeSlidesRoot` assigns `root.slides = document.slides` verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:104), so `slides[i].elements[j].text.blocks[k].inlines[l].style.color = null` (or `{kind:'srgb',value:42}`) is persisted unchanged. Every client that renders the deck reaches `resolveStoredColor` from `paintLayout` (packages/docs/src/view/paint-layout.ts:388, 453, 555), `table-renderer.ts:464/573` and `resolveColorAtPosition` (color.ts:182) and throws, so the canvas render loop dies for all collaborators until the poisoned value is removed out-of-band. Fix: make the guard total (`typeof c !== 'object' || c === null` → false; `typeof c.value === 'string' && c.value.trim() === ''`).

samples.summary: The newly added `assertValidBlockStyle` alignment gate is bypassable: docs `header`/`footer` blocks and docs blocks embedded in slide text elements are persisted verbatim without ever passing through `assertValidBlock`, so the API-level 'no arbitrary alignment enters the document' guarantee stated in its docstring does not hold.
samples.evidence: `assertValidDocsBody` (controller.ts:239-252) walks only `body.blocks` (and, via `assertValidBlock`, nested table-cell blocks). But `writeDocsRoot`→`buildTreeChildren` also persists `document.header.blocks` and `document.footer.blocks` through `buildBlockNode` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:289-305), and `serializeBlockStyle` copies `style.alignment` verbatim into the Yorkie attribute (docs-tree.ts:143). So `PUT {"blocks":[],"header":{"marginFromEdge":0,"blocks":[{"id":"x","type":"paragraph","style":{"alignment":"center\"/><w:jc w:val=\"right"},"inlines":[]}]}}` stores exactly the string the new test claims is rejected, and it is exported into `word/header1.xml` (packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:360-382 → `buildParagraphPropertiesXml`). The same hole exists for the slides arm: `assertValidElement` (controller.ts:415) checks only `id`/`type`/`frame`, and `writeSlidesRoot` assigns `root.slides` verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:104), so `elements[].text.blocks[].style.alignment` is unvalidated. Impact is currently contained because both export sinks clamp (`DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` in docx-style-map.ts:141, `ALGN[...] ?? 'l'` in packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:79) — but the guard reads as covering the input surface when it covers only one of three writer paths.

samples.summary: `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS[style.alignment as string]` is an object-literal lookup, so it is not actually a closed map: inherited `Object.prototype` keys resolve instead of falling back to the default, and any prototype-pollution gadget turns this 'injection-proof by construction' sink back into raw interpolation into `<w:jc w:val>`.
samples.evidence: `const DOCX_ALIGNMENTS: Record<string,string> = { left, center, right, justify }` (docx-style-map.ts:115-120) inherits from `Object.prototype`, so `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS['constructor']`, `['toString']`, `['__proto__']`, `['hasOwnProperty']` etc. are truthy and skip the `?? 'left'` default. With `style.alignment === 'constructor'` (persistable via the unvalidated header/footer or slides paths above) line 143 emits `<w:jc w:val="function Object() { [native code] }"/>` — schema-invalid OOXML rather than the intended default. Built-in values happen to contain no `"`/`<`, so this alone is not an escape, but the guarantee the comment claims ('can only ever carry an ST_Jc token') is false, and a single `Object.prototype` write anywhere in the bundle (a merge/deep-assign gadget) makes it an attribute-injection sink. Use `Object.hasOwn(DOCX_ALIGNMENTS, v) ? ... : 'left'`, a `Map`, or `Object.create(null)`. The same pattern exists pre-existing at packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:79 (`ALGN[...] ?? 'l'`) and packages/slides/src/export/pptx/shape.ts:63 (`DASH_VAL[...]`), which this delta's comment now cites as the model to mirror.

mergedFrom.summary: DOCX attribute injection via `style.alignment`: the sibling sink in the very function this change hardened is still interpolated raw into `<w:jc w:val="..."/>`

finding.summary: `style.alignment` is interpolated unescaped and unvalidated into `<w:jc w:val="…">` — the same OOXML attribute-injection sink class this change hardens for colors, three lines below the fixed code
finding.evidence: buildParagraphPropertiesXml does `const align = style.alignment === 'justify' ? 'both' : style.alignment;` then `parts.push(`<w:jc w:val="${align}"/>`)` for anything that is not the literal 'left' (docx-style-map.ts:123-126). Unlike `fontFamily` (escaped at line 70-71) and now `color`/`backgroundColor` (normalized at 95/99), `align` gets neither escaping nor an allowlist. BlockStyle.alignment is typed as a closed union, but the runtime value comes from the Yorkie tree attributes with an unchecked cast: `partial.alignment = attrs.alignment as BlockStyle['alignment']` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:220), and `normalizeBlockStyle` only spreads defaults (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272-274) — no validation anywhere on that path. Attack: a collaborator with write access to a shared doc (or anything writing the tree attr, incl. the backend docs-tree serializer) sets the block attribute `alignment` to `center"/><w:pStyle w:val="x` (or `a" w:x="`); when any other user exports the document, DocxExporter emits that string verbatim into word/document.xml (and header1.xml/footer1.xml via buildHeaderFooterXml), closing the `<w:jc>` element and injecting attacker-chosen OOXML into a file other users open in Word. Note the PPTX exporter does allowlist the same field (`ALGN[block.style.alignment] ?? 'l'`, packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:79), which is the pattern missing here. Confidence is medium only because I could not confirm the Yorkie server accepts an arbitrary `alignment` attribute value from a peer client; the exporter-side sink itself is unambiguous.

searchedFor: grep 'ALIGNMENTS|isAlignment|alignment ===|validAlign' across all packages/**/src (only layout.ts, the toolbar, and the docx export ternary match — no validator)
read normalizeBlockStyle (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272) — plain spread, no validation
grep 'w:fill=|w:color=|w:val="${|srgbClr val=' across **/src/**/*.ts to enumerate every OOXML attribute sink
finding.summary: The docs content PUT API validates only the *shape* of `style`, not its values, so arbitrary strings persist into the CRDT and reach unescaped OOXML attribute sinks
finding.evidence:
`assertValidBlock` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:254-306) checks `id`, `type`, that `style` is an object, and array-ness of `inlines`/`tableData.rows`/`cells` — deliberately, per its own comment, "just the fields the writer unconditionally dereferences". No block-style or inline-style value is validated. `writeDocsRoot` then persists them verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:143, 174-184).

This is the enabling half of the `w:jc` injection above and is the reason that fixing only the color sinks leaves the class open: every current and future string-valued style field that an exporter interpolates is attacker-controlled. Surveyed the whole DOCX/PPTX attribute surface for other reachable string sinks — `fontFamily` is escaped (docx-style-map.ts:70-73, pptx text.ts:300), `headingLevel` is coerced with `Number()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:438, docs-tree.ts:409) so at worst yields `Heading NaN`, `verticalAlign`/`borderStyle` are cast unchecked (yorkie-doc-store.ts:251,257) but the DOCX table writer emits no `vAlign`/`tcBorders` (docx-exporter.ts:301-323), `image.src` never enters XML (only the zip + an internally generated rId), and DOCX emits no hyperlinks at all — so `alignment` is the one live string sink today. Validating style values at the trust boundary (or per-sink allowlists) would make that robust rather than incidental.
